issue: FIX: F03 remains incomplete: an OSError during waiting or reaping returns a started engine record without confirming containment, bypassing the survivor check and permitting snapshotting and gates beside surviving children. Guarantee cleanup on every post-creation exit and halt when cleanup cannot be confirmed; test a reap failure with a living descendant.
reason: Refuted by an executed adversarial verification: runner.py:312-317 orders _start -> ProcessTree -> _exit_within -> reap -> read_text, so the only post-creation OSError site (log.read_text) runs after reap has SIGTERM'd, SIGKILL'd and settled the group; Popen.wait swallows ChildProcessError and _probe/_signal catch ProcessLookupError/PermissionError, so waiting and reaping raise no OSError; Win32Error is a RuntimeError, not an OSError. A cmd engine that spawned a TERM-ignoring grandchild and then deleted its own out.txt returned launch=started with the grandchild gone and the process group empty. The existing test that reaches the branch monkeypatches reap itself. Residual (not a concrete input): a SIGKILL survivor plus a read_text failure is a double fault an unprivileged engine cannot produce.
